partition.krs-grammar-partition:
KRS-PART-SYNTAX (program syntax)
  sort Exp
  sort Value
  subsort Value ::= Int
  subsort Value ::= Bool
  subsort Exp ::= Value
  production ExpSyntax::And
  production ExpSyntax::Neg
KRS-PART (pub productions that are not program syntax)
  (none)
partition.krs-grammar-kevm-case:
KRS-EVM-SYNTAX (program syntax)
  sort Command
  sort LogEntry
  production Commands::Done
  production Commands::Emit
KRS-EVM (pub productions that are not program syntax)
  production BlockHashLookup: argument `hashes: List`: K has no LIST-SYNTAX module
  production LogRecord::Entry: argument `topics: List`: K has no LIST-SYNTAX module
partition.krs-grammar-program-warning:
KRS-PROGRAM-WARNING-SYNTAX (program syntax)
  sort LogEntry
KRS-PROGRAM-WARNING (pub productions that are not program syntax)
  production LogRecord::Entry: argument `topics: List`: K has no LIST-SYNTAX module

krs-grammar-program-warning: warning[krs::partition::not-program-syntax]: `LogRecord::Entry` is marked `program` but its field `topics: List` needs K's LIST module, which has no -SYNTAX variant; it is placed in KRS-PROGRAM-WARNING and programs cannot contain it

removed-root: error[krs::plan::removed-facet-key]: could not plan collector: package `krs-grammar-removed-root` definition `main` sets `root`: the key was removed; program syntax is now `pub` minus `internal`
removed-syntax-root: error[krs::plan::removed-facet-key]: could not plan collector: package `krs-grammar-removed-syntax-root` definition `main` sets `syntax-root`: the key was removed; program syntax is now `pub` minus `internal`
invalid-int-literals: error[krs::plan::invalid-int-literals]: could not plan collector: package `krs-grammar-invalid-int-literals` sets `int-literals = "natural"`; expected "signed" (the default, INT-SYNTAX) or "unsigned" (UNSIGNED-INT-SYNTAX)
internal-not-pub: error[krs::expand::invalid-placement-flag]: `internal` applies only to a `pub` production; non-pub productions are already private
mixed-group: error[krs::partition::mixed-group]: group `ops_tier0` mixes `internal` production `Ops::Hidden` with program-syntax production `Ops::Visible`; K priorities and associativity apply per module, so mark both `internal` or neither
signed-leak: error[krs::partition::signed-integer-leak]: `KRS-UNSIGNED-ROOT-SYNTAX` uses `int-literals = "unsigned"` but imports `KRS-SIGNED-BASE-SYNTAX`, whose signed INT-SYNTAX literals would leak into programs (K imports are unions)
colors-mismatch: error[krs::syntax::invalid-color]: invalid production colours: `colors` needs one colour per terminal of the syntax template plus one per `%c`
prefer-avoid: error[krs::syntax::invalid-argument-value]: `prefer` must be omitted: a production is either preferred or avoided, not both
overload-arity: error[krs::analysis::invalid-overload]: invalid `overload`: `LValSyntax::LvalField` takes 1 argument but its target `ExpSyntax::Dot` takes 2 arguments; an overload has the target's arity
overload-not-subsort: error[krs::analysis::invalid-overload]: invalid `overload`: `LValSyntax::LvalDot` does not specialise `ExpSyntax::Dot`: its sort `Id` is not a subsort of `Int`
overload-cycle: error[krs::analysis::invalid-overload]: invalid `overload`: the overload targets form a cycle: `ExpSyntax::Dot` -> `LValSyntax::LvalDot` -> `ExpSyntax::Dot`
visibility-claim: error[krs::analysis::private-production-in-spec]: `Helper::Wrap` is private to KRS-VISIBILITY-CLAIM; K's private syntax is invisible to proof modules. Make it `pub` and mark it `internal`
token-constructor: error[krs::analysis::invalid-token-sort]: `NameSyntax::Anonymous` is a constructor of `Name`, a token sort: a sort with domain values has no constructors; give the constructor another sort, or use a function
lexeme-not-token: error[krs::analysis::invalid-token-sort]: `k::lexeme!(Stmt, "halt")` names `Stmt`, which is not a token sort; declare its tokens with `#[k::token(..)]` on a `struct Stmt(String);`
lexeme-builtin: error[krs::analysis::invalid-token-sort]: `k::lexeme!` names the builtin sort `Int`; write a builtin token as a literal, `k::id!("$name")`, or `k::bytes!(b"..")`
token-duplicate: error[krs::analysis::invalid-token-sort]: the token terminal "main" is declared twice on sort `Name`; each token production of a sort is declared once
token-alias-builtin: error[krs::analysis::invalid-token-sort]: a `#[k::token]` type alias adds token productions to a user sort or to builtin `Id`; `Int` has its own domain values, written as literals
lexical-duplicate: error[krs::analysis::duplicate-lexical]: the lexical `Alpha` is declared more than once; K names lexicals in one namespace per definition, so rename one
lexical-undefined: error[krs::analysis::undefined-lexical]: the token regex "{Alpha}{Digit}*" refers to `{Digit}`, which no `k::lexical!` declares; declare it with `k::lexical! { Digit = r".."; }` or escape the brace as `\{`
lexical-recursive: error[krs::analysis::recursive-lexical]: lexicals refer to each other in a cycle (`Tail` -> `Word` -> `Tail`); K expands `{Name}` references inline, so a lexical cannot reach itself
list-collision: error[krs::analysis::symbol-name-collision]: syntactic list `Ints` derives the symbols `intsCons`/`intsNil`, which collide with `IntsCons`; rename the enum or the other production
list-constructor: error[krs::analysis::invalid-syntax-list]: `IntsSyntax::Empty` constructs `Ints`, a syntactic list: a `#[k::syntax_list]` enum is the whole definition of its sort, so the list has no other constructors; give the constructor another sort, or use a function
overload-overlap: error[krs::analysis::overlapping-rule-heads]: rules `general` and `specific` can both apply to the same configuration at the same priority; K would take either one (nondeterminism). If that is intended, put both in one group with `#[k::rule(nondet = NAME)]`; otherwise refine a pattern, add disjoint `where` sorts or complementary requires guards, or order them with `owise` or `priority = N`.
list-value-not-strict: error[krs::analysis::invalid-syntax-list]: `Vals` is declared a subsort of `Exps`, a syntactic list that is not strict: only a strict list admits a subsort, its value list
list-value-result: error[krs::analysis::invalid-syntax-list]: `Vals` is the value list of `Exps`, but `Vals` is not a subsort of `KResult`, the strictness result of `Exps`: declare it in `k::sorts!`, as in `impl KResult for Vals;`
token-private-field: error[krs::analysis::invalid-token-sort]: `StmtSyntax::Call` is program syntax, but every token production of `Name`, the sort of its field `target`, is private, so no program can contain it. Make the `#[k::token]` carrier of `Name` `pub`, or take `StmtSyntax::Call` out of program syntax: make it non-`pub`, or mark it `internal`
token-k-regex: error[krs::analysis::token-collision]: the token regex r"[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9]*" at `prec(0)` is the regex of K's own `#LowerId` token, which K declares at `prec(2)`; K keys a regex token by its text, so Java K and k-rust both reject the definition. Use a different regex, or `prec = 2`
token-cell-name: error[krs::analysis::token-collision]: the token regex r"[a-z][a-z0-9_]*" at `prec(2)` lexes `k`, the name of the configuration cell `<k>`, at least as strongly as K's own `#LowerId` token (`prec(2)`), so Java K cannot parse the emitted configuration. Lower its `prec` below 2, or change the regex so it does not match `k`
configuration-visibility: error[krs::partition::configuration-visibility]: the rules of `KRS-CONFIGURATION-VISIBILITY-BASE` need the configuration, so it is emitted in `KRS-CONFIGURATION-VISIBILITY-CONFIGURATION`, which cannot import the configured package's semantics module or any module that imports it; the configuration names `modeSyntaxReady`, which is declared outside the modules `KRS-CONFIGURATION-VISIBILITY-CONFIGURATION` imports, so make `modeSyntaxReady` program syntax (`pub`, not `internal`) or move the rules of `KRS-CONFIGURATION-VISIBILITY-BASE` into the configured package
symbol-variant-struct: error[krs::analysis::symbol-name-collision]: emitted symbol name collision for "opAdd" between production `Op::Add` of KRS-SYMBOL-VARIANT-STRUCT (enum `Op` + variant `Add`) and production `OpAdd` of KRS-SYMBOL-VARIANT-STRUCT
symbol-generated: error[krs::analysis::symbol-name-collision]: production `IsExp` of KRS-SYMBOL-GENERATED has the symbol "isExp", which K generates as the sort predicate of `Exp`
symbol-explicit: error[krs::analysis::symbol-name-collision]: emitted symbol name collision for "same" between production `One` of KRS-SYMBOL-EXPLICIT (pinned by `#[k::symbol("second::Same")]`) and production `ExpSyntax::Zero` of KRS-SYMBOL-EXPLICIT (pinned by `#[k::symbol("first::Same")]`)
